Mark is an investor, trader and trading performance specialist with 13 years’ experience in the markets. His experience spans a multitude of assets and markets, as well as longer-term investing, swing trading, intraday trading and scalping, giving him first-hand understanding of the different psychological, technical and risk demands each trading style creates. Alongside his market experience, Mark brings 18 years of professional experience helping people understand and change deeply ingrained, detrimental and self-destructive patterns of behaviour.

That experience now sits alongside serious market education: technical analysis, strategy development, structured risk management and the behavioural work required to execute those things under pressure.

The Spartan Story. Before Stoic Spartan, Mark spent 18 years working across rehabilitation centres, prisons and various communities, where he provided support and worked directly with more than 1,500 individuals, helping people understand and change deeply ingrained behavioural patterns. That work is where the Spartan story began. Read The Spartan Story →

“The gap between what you know and what you actually do is where I do some of my best work.”

— Mark

Mark is not there simply to tell a trader what they are doing wrong. He starts by understanding what is actually happening — what the trader does, when it happens, what happens immediately before it, and what the behaviour is giving them. From there, the pattern can be challenged honestly and something practical can be put in its place.

Empathy without collusion.

Mark helps traders understand why certain decisions, reactions and behavioural patterns emerge during execution. Once the underlying pattern is properly understood, practical solutions can be put in place. After all, before any problem can be solved effectively, it first needs to be understood.

Challenge without humiliation.

Contradictions, rationalisations and destructive behavioural patterns are identified early and explored without judgement. Once recognised, the trader can begin putting the necessary solutions, processes and guardrails in place so those patterns no longer continue to undermine execution and performance.

Responsibility without shame.

Mark helps traders take responsibility for the things within their control without allowing guilt, shame or embarrassment to become another barrier to progress. The trader can own what happened, learn from it and change it. The markets cannot be controlled. The work begins with learning to control what can be controlled — starting with ourselves.

Independence over dependency.

The goal is not to make the trader reliant on mentorship. It is to help them become increasingly capable of seeing, understanding and correcting their own behaviour through structured processes of self-analysis, reflection and continued self-improvement.

How Mark Works With Traders

Insight matters. Changed behaviour matters more.

01 Understand what is actually happening

Not simply “you are undisciplined”. What exactly is happening? When does it happen? What comes immediately before it? Mark slows the sequence down until the actual behaviour — and the trigger behind it — becomes visible.

02 Challenge the story

Is the market really the problem? Is this genuinely an exception? Would the trader advise somebody else to do the same thing? Mark tests the explanation, exposes contradictions and challenges the story where the evidence does not support it.

03 Identify the pattern

What is the behaviour providing — relief, control, excitement, revenge, hope or avoidance? Mark looks for the repeated pattern and the function it is serving, because behaviour becomes easier to change once its purpose is understood.

04 Put something practical in its place

Rules, guard rails, environmental changes, accountability, planned responses and clear actions are put in place. The objective is not merely to understand the problem, but to give the trader something better to do when it appears again.

05 Test it under pressure

Insight when calm is not the same as changed behaviour when money is on the line. The new response is tested, reviewed and refined until it can hold up under genuine trading pressure.

“Often, it’s difficult to see the wood for the trees when you’re standing in the middle of them. I have the advantage of being objective — as if I’m looking down on the forest from a helicopter. I can often see where you’ve drifted from the path, what keeps pulling you away from it, and help you navigate through the forest towards greater consistency, improved performance and ultimately, success.”

The Stoic Spartan Trifecta

Why technical analysis alone is not enough.

If successful trading were simply a matter of learning charts, indicators and setups, there would be vastly more consistently profitable traders.

One study of persistent Brazilian equity-futures day traders found that 97% lost money after trading for more than 300 days. European regulatory analysis has also reported that 74–89% of retail CFD accounts typically lose money.1–2

These figures describe specific populations, not every trader in every market. Their relevance is the same: technical competence alone does not guarantee professional performance.

Technical AnalysisIdentifies opportunity.

Risk ManagementProtects the capital and keeps you in the game.

Trading PsychologyDetermines whether you can execute the edge consistently when money and emotion are involved.

The Method

Three disciplines. One professional operating system.

The aim is not to collect more information. It is to make better decisions, protect capital and execute those decisions under pressure.

01

Develop The Edge

Technical Analysis

Understand the environment before reaching for an entry. Read location, value, structure, momentum and behaviour together, then use additional evidence to build context and confirmation.

  • Stop forcing setups in poor environments
  • Distinguish confirmation from anticipation
  • Recognise trend, rotation and transition
  • Build repeatable continuation and reversal models
Environment→Location→Context→Confirmation→Risk→Execution

Context & confirmation: Order Blocks • Liquidity • Fair Value Gaps • Candlestick Formations • Chart Patterns • Volume • and much more.

Market Structure • Auction Market Theory • VWAP • Volume Profile • Order Flow • Institutional Price Action • Imbalances • Multi-Timeframe Analysis • Trend • Rotation • Momentum • Trade Planning

02

Protect The Capital

Risk Management

Professional traders survive first, then compound. Risk has to be designed before emotion gets involved.

  • Correctly size the position
  • Stop increasing risk after losses
  • Build hard daily loss and drawdown rules
  • Scale without turning progress into a boom-and-bust cycle

Position Sizing • Scaling • Trade Management • Drawdown Control • Risk-to-Reward • Prop-Firm Rules • Capital Preservation

03

Master The Trader

Trading Psychology

The greatest edge is often invisible: the capacity to execute what you already know when uncertainty, money and emotion collide.

  • Break revenge trading and loss chasing
  • Stop cutting winners simply to relieve anxiety
  • Control FOMO, hesitation and impulsivity
  • Build confidence from process rather than outcome

Discipline • Emotional Control • Patience • Self-Awareness • Accountability • Decision-Making Under Pressure • Performance Habits

Technical Analysis Mastery

Learn to read the market. Build the edge. Execute the framework.

Stoic Spartan teaches technical analysis across strategies, systems, markets and timeframes. Traders learn to read market behaviour, understand context and location, and build or refine a framework that can be explained, tested and repeated — rather than relying on isolated indicators or borrowed setups.

Environment→Location→Context→Confirmation→Risk→Execution
01 Read the environment before looking for the trade

Mark teaches traders to establish the market environment first: structure, trend, rotation, value, momentum and the broader auction. Market Structure, Auction Market Theory, VWAP, Volume Profile, Order Flow and Multi-Timeframe Analysis are used to answer a more important question than “where is the entry?” — what kind of market is this?

02 Understand location and where the trade actually makes sense

Good analysis is not only directional. It is also locational. Traders learn to identify meaningful areas of value, imbalance and liquidity, distinguish premium locations from poor ones, and stop forcing setups in the middle of nowhere.

03 Build context and confirmation — not a collection of magic signals

Order Blocks, Liquidity, Fair Value Gaps, Candlestick Formations, Chart Patterns, Volume, and much more can all add useful evidence. They are taught as additional context and confirmation — not isolated reasons to enter a trade. Institutional Price Action, Imbalances, momentum and behaviour are combined with the environment and location already established.

04 Build or refine a strategy that suits the trader and timeframe

Different traders need different frameworks. Mark can help build or refine continuation and reversal models, entry triggers, invalidation, targets, trade-management rules and multi-timeframe processes across different styles and timeframes. The objective is a strategy the trader can explain, test and repeat — not a borrowed setup they barely understand.

05 Integrate risk and execution into the technical framework

A technical edge is incomplete without a risk framework. Position sizing, stop placement, invalidation, daily-loss limits, drawdown control and trade management are integrated before execution. Psychology then serves the final task: helping the trader follow the technical and risk process when money and pressure are real.

FAQ

What you should know before joining or applying.

Do you provide trading signals?

No. Stoic Spartan is not a signal service and does not issue trade alerts or tell members what they should buy or sell. During Stoic Spartan Live, Mark may analyse markets and trade his own account in real time, explaining the market context, strategy, risk and decision-making behind what he is doing. Members make their own independent trading decisions. Any trading shown during a live session is educational and should not be treated as a recommendation or instruction to copy a trade. Trading involves substantial risk.

What is the difference between Stoic Spartan Live, Core, Pro and Elite?

Stoic Spartan Live is the group-access doorway into the Stoic Spartan environment. Core is the entry point into private mentorship, adding personal 1-to-1 development across Technical Analysis, Risk Management and Trading Psychology alongside ongoing direct support. Pro is a more intensive private mentorship pathway, with weekly live 1-to-1 sessions, closer ongoing contact and deeper individual analysis and accountability. Elite is the most comprehensive and bespoke Stoic Spartan mentorship pathway. It is not reserved for advanced traders: the programme begins at the individual's current level and is built around the areas that will create the greatest progression — from Technical Analysis and strategy development to execution, Trading Psychology, Risk Management, processes and funded-trader development. Core, Pro and Elite all include the complete Stoic Spartan Live membership while mentorship is active.

What markets are covered?

The principles apply across futures, indices, NASDAQ, S&P 500, gold, silver, forex and crypto, including Micro Nasdaq, Micro S&P 500, Micro Gold and Micro Silver futures. The exact technical focus can be adapted to the trader and instrument.

Are profits, funding or payouts guaranteed?

No. Trading involves substantial risk. Coaching can improve process, knowledge, decision-making and discipline, but no legitimate programme can guarantee a trading outcome.
